body.statement: A finite multigraph \(G\) contains \(q\) pairwise edge-disjoint spanning trees if and only if every partition of \(V\) into \(m\) nonempty parts has at least \(q(m-1)\) edges joining distinct parts.

source.verbatim_statement: A theorem due independently to Tutte and Nash-Williams characterizes the maximum number of edge-wise disjoint connected spanning subgraphs into which the edges can be partitioned.

upstream.citation: Nash-Williams, C. St. J. A. (1961). Edge-disjoint spanning trees of finite graphs.

attestation.note: Verified through the lawful public-domain Edmonds 1965 NBS Part II source, page 73, which explicitly attributes the connected-spanning-subgraph characterization to the cited 1961 Nash-Williams paper; spanning trees are obtained by choosing a tree in each connected spanning part. [marker acknowledged: Nash-Williams attribution in the verifying Edmonds source]
